episodes.173791: A strong surface low developed and led to strong winds, record warmth, severe thunderstorms, and grass fires. Peak observed winds were between 60 - 70 mph. A few hail reports were also received.
episodes.174075: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed into eastern Oklahoma on the 24th, as a cold front moved into the region. The strongest thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.174354: A squall line advanced across South Central Minnesota during the late evening of Sunday, October 23rd. An isolated strong wind gust of 54 knots was recorded at the Redwood Falls Airport ASOS station just after 0200 UTC. As the line continued northeastward, storms continued to develop, however they remained sub-severe with gusty winds and small hail.
episodes.174419: A weak EF-0 tornado occurred in rural Woodburn with minor damage.
episodes.174504: Very strong deep-layer shear developed as a result of an increase in the low-level jet and turning mid-level winds ahead of the approaching strong upper-level trough. A strong push of mid-level instability created up to 1000 J/kg MUCAPE, despite an environment with a strong sub-cloud dry layer.  Storms moved rapidly northeast, with a cluster of hail producing storms in east central South Dakota. A second round of wind-producing storms erupted on the nose of the low-level jet across far northeast Nebraska, and translated quickly through southeast South Dakota into northwest Iowa and southwest Minnesota. |Strong synoptic winds were observed well to the north of the storms toward the southeast side of the Sioux Falls metro area with some reports of wind damage.

episodes.174809: A line of thunderstorms crosses the area during the morning of the 24th with minor wind damage and a couple of tornadoes reported embedded within the line.
episodes.174949: An upper low and a cold front led to the development of showers and thunderstorms across North and Central Texas on October 24. A few storms developed in the morning as a lead disturbance moved overhead. Most storms occurred in the evening, however, as the front pushed through the area. A few of these storms became severe, producing both large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.174980: Scattered thunderstorms produced a few severe weather reports during the afternoon across the Big Country and Heartland.

events.narrative: A thunderstorm wind gust of 63 mph was measured by South Dakota State University mesonet site BFMS2 7 miles west-southwest of Beresford.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 66 mph was measured by South Dakota Road Weather Information System site SD508 3 miles south-southwest of Beresford.
Personal weather station measured a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
Numerous one to three-inch tree limbs were broken off by thunderstorm wind gusts.
Three-inch diameter tree branches were downed by thunderstorm wind gusts.
Winds gusts were measured by a personal weather station.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 74 mph was measured by Minnesota Road Weather Information System site MN147 near Magnolia.
Strong thunderstorm wind gusts plastered leaves all over the side of the house, and knocked out power.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 62 mph was measured by Minnesota Road Weather Information System site MN038 3 miles west of Dovray.
Estimated winds of 50-60 mph were reported in northeast Jack County.

The tornado initially broke some tree branches along State Highway 152 between Gregory Road and Banner Road, then moved east-northeast producing more tree damage and roof damage on the north side of a residence on Richland Road north of SH-152.
The Emergency Manager reported damage to buildings in and around Paradise. The damage consisted of garage door being blown in.
Spotter network report of 60 mph winds in Decatur.
Tree damage was reported on Dutton Road south of Banner Road.
Emergency management spotters reported a brief tornado near US Highway 177 and State Highway 59B. No damage was reported.
The Oklahoma Mesonet station near Porter measured 59 mph thunderstorm wind gusts.
Also, there were reported wind gusts between 40 and 58 mph in Rule.

A weak tornado occurred in rural Woodburn, confirmed by video and supported by damage photos obtained from the public. Rated EF-0 with winds estimated between 61-74 mph. Damage to two residential properties.
